intro: A retired Navy admiral comes home quietly after ten years away, only to be picked as a scapegoat by the police chief who is dating his sister, the state governor. It plays like a page-turner thriller novel, now on screen: a corrupt man who thinks he owns the streets and the system, a family dinner that is supposed to make everyone look good, and one quiet stranger nobody bothered to check. The fun is in waiting for the room to find out who he really is.
why: A hidden-identity story where the audience knows the truth long before the villains do.
A sharp sibling bond: the governor raised her little brother, and he still puts her first.
A villain built on arrogance, the kind of character you watch just to see him fall.
Good pick if you like revenge stories, power reveals and justice that arrives slowly, then all at once.

faq.q: What is My Sister's Boyfriend Arrested Me about?
faq.a: Arthur, a retired Navy admiral, returns home to see his sister Eleanor, the governor. Her new boyfriend, Police Chief Gavin Mercer, is under pressure to close a case and decides any stranger will do as a scapegoat. He has no idea who he just stopped.

faq.q: Is My Sister's Boyfriend Arrested Me worth watching?
faq.a: If you enjoy hidden identities and corrupt villains getting what they deserve, yes. It leans on tension and payoff rather than romance.
Arthur, the admiral who keeps his rank to himself; Eleanor, his older sister and the state governor; and Gavin Mercer, the police chief who believes his family owns the city.
